description: Exactly what the shell's own page needs, and nothing more. That page is the app's first-run and diagnostics surface (`dist/index.html`) — the only document that runs on the shell's own origin — and it only calls `desktop_info`, `recent_logs`, `set_database_url`, `restart_server` and `open_data_dir`, plus the sidecar event stream. The app permission set in `permissions/default.toml` is limited to those five commands; the `core:event` rules are the listen and the unlisten `listen` hands back. The process, opener, dialog, os, fs and store plugins are not granted to any local document: the page opens no URL, picks no file, reads no file and never touches the preference store directly. The shell does all of that in Rust, where the ACL does not gate it. In particular, `tauri-plugin-store` performs no scope check of its own, and the store it keeps is only for non-secret preferences — the database URL and session secret live in the encrypted `secrets.bin` store, not there.
